title: Rabbi Zekharyah ben Kevutal
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a great man in Temple times, as in Mishnah Yoma 1:6, where he said: “Many times I read before him (before the High Priest on the night of Yom Kippur) from Daniel.” Hyman argues that this does not prove that he was a Kohen, for in the Mishnah there they said that if the High Priest cannot expound, Torah scholars expound before him; so he could even be an Israelite. But from Berakhot 63a, where they said that the sages sent to Chananya, the nephew of Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Yose ben Kifar and the son of Rabbi Zekharyah ben Kevutal, and he proclaimed concerning them that they were the great men of the generation and their fathers had served in the Temple — Hyman infers from this that he was a Kohen.
In Yoma 19b: “Rav Chanan bar Rava taught Chiyya bar Rav: Zekharyah ben Kefutal, and Rav pointed with his hand: Kevutal.” The Jerusalem Talmud there reads Kevutar.

notes.text: Chananya is not labeled a heretic: the older unsupported note is withdrawn in the current edition, with prior versions preserved. Hyman says son; saved Davidson Berakhot63a explicitly has grandson of Zekharyah. His priesthood inference is retained as his argument, not a newly proven genealogy.
